Negative numeric delta observed for Move, Toughness, Attacks and Strength.

Each model in the rules unit receives the same recorded result as its actual Normal Move budget. The test uses a constructed characteristic and explicit selection checkpoint.

Five healing points affect only the named model and leave the other wounded model at one.
The model-scoped effect completes after restoring one wound, discarding the remaining four.
The destroyed unit member remains at zero after the named model is healed and the effect completes.
The native heal finishes with current and initial Wounds both equal to two, the known profile value for that case. No generalized dynamic-W modification proof is claimed.

Explicit Core input grants +1 A once to each of two equipped Ranger ranged profiles. Actual attack generation returns base plus one per ranged weapon, excludes melee mutation and produces no fixed-profile roll. Datasheet-provider admission is outside this witness.

Weapon/profile rows precede submission and source identity is consumed by the declaration. Weapons and targets commit together in the facade. A separate accepted weapon-to-target transition is outside these assertions.
The actual declaration fixes targets before attack steps. The split facade verifies the target-resolution choice and absence of attack steps after declaration and before group resolution.
Both facades assert no resolution before declaration, then real steps and completed sequences for the declared physical weapons.
Actual Fight completes with the declared physical profile; the separate native melee owner asserts melee range identity for every resulting pool, including a target split.
Native Chaos Spawn can select and complete normal shooting with no ranged declaration or attack step and no shot status.
A native body with explicitly empty equipment activates and completes Fight with no attack step or participation. This confirms the conditional Core path at the constructed checkpoint.
Two profiles of one physical plasma pistol are rejected atomically, followed by both single-profile legal retries in separate variants.
Two native Noise Marine bearers separately choose distinct Blastmaster profiles and keep their exact physical weapon and bearer identities in accepted pools.

Completed Shooting and Fight pools carry the whole source weapon profile, including characteristic and ability fields, and fixed A. The timing of individual weapon ability activation is handled by the owning ability cases.
Selected shooter ID and pending typed declaration exist before any attack step; the dedicated guard also proves selection/declaration does not count as shot.
Legal Fight activation emits selection and opens a typed melee declaration before any attack step.
One target is retained for each used physical ranged weapon, including split unit declarations. Friendly targets and duplicate physical weapon commitments are rejected.
Native out-of-range target is rejected and the selected shooting type finishes with no attacks, no shot and continued unit selection.
With legal targets present, the optional empty and targetless submissions complete with no attack delta and no shot.

The native one-target and split variants preserve target cardinality in initial pools and completed declaration evidence. Neither asserts a downstream rule consuming the model- or unit-level single-target predicate.
Both phases assign fixed A to each pool and the three-weapon shooting executor records exactly that many hit steps for each physical weapon.
Native target-group sequence uses all pool indices; physical grouped contributions and result-driven group discharge use the finished executor state in both phases.
A partly resolved multi-weapon sequence rejects full completion; both facades and the three-weapon case complete only after declared pools are all used.
Ranged weapon completion is independently retained after all attacks in its single-target pool finish, while another weapon and the model/unit remain incomplete.
Both Shooting and Fight finish one bearer, hold the other pending, and recognize the finished model before whole-sequence completion. Native bodies and selected-pool executor contract.
Real facade declaration is pending before attacks with no completion event and unit not shot. Executor distinguishes partial weapon completion from full sequence. These are bounded boundary controls.
Declined legal targets, no legal targets and the native weaponless shooter finish selection without entering the shot inventory.

Completion is asserted for a native melee physical pool and the split declaration conserves its attacks. The controls do not join a single weapon split across targets with the later weapon completion transition.
Both Shooting and Fight finish one bearer, hold the other pending, and recognize the finished model before whole-sequence completion. Native bodies and selected-pool executor contract.

The positive native unit-has-fought event follows attack resolution, and the no-attack activation emits none. An in-flight, nonempty multi-model Fight unit-has-fought negative assertion is still absent from this family.
Real facade completion, plus direct all-attacks boundary evidence across a pending target reaction, distinguish finished attacks from earlier group consumption or later continuation.
Native Chaos Spawn selects normal shooting and completes that type with no attack declaration or shot.

A zero-equipment native body proves the conditional Fight activation can complete without attacks or fought status. The historical shooting-only link cannot establish this clause. The current constructed Fight control supplies it.
For the native 3-attack pool all d6 records for each hit, wound and save step precede the first resolution record of that step. The fixture controls faces.
The last hit outcome precedes the first wound outcome, including a three-attack pool, and a failed hit yields no wound roll.
The successful native single-attack path loses one wound and completes. A three-attack lethal case records one damage step, destroys the final target and discards remaining attacks.
Direct executor completion is asserted for hit, wound and save failures, resolved damaging attacks, and completion on destruction of the only target.
The hit spec requests 1D6 for native ranged and melee profiles. Face sweeps validate the physical face and one pool test counts one recorded hit die per attack.
A 1D6 wound spec and per-step recorded die counts distinguish hits requiring a roll from failures that stop earlier.
Unmodified one fails all tested thresholds and modifiers, even where a modified total would otherwise reach the target.
Unmodified six is critical in every threshold and modifier case in the default rule contract.
The S4 native profile with constructed Toughness boundaries checks every physical face against the required threshold and modifiers -1, 0 and +1, with natural one and six handled separately.
Identical native non-Characters form one group. A separately changed W, Sv or InSv produces two groups with exact memberships.
Every legal order places the two wounded groups before the unwounded group and actual casualty mutation advances to the next live group.
Native D1 removes one wound after a failed save. A two-pool post-wound contract supplies recorded D1 and D2, accepts either order through the real selector, and removes three wounds in total.
Native save faces and AP establish failed-save outcomes. The sequence applies only the expected failure damage and the Resolve Damage FNP case distinguishes ignored wounds.

Resolve Damage still occurs when D is replaced by zero or FNP ignores a wound. These tests assert the authoritative step and wound totals. A separately admitted downstream suffers-damage rule is unasserted.

Retained attack completion or expiry removes the casualty. Ordinary non-retained destruction reacts before removal. The adopted FAQ20 exception separately proves after-removal Deadly Demise. A retained non-Demise destruction rule followed by removal remains outside these cases.

The authenticated retained native Lord can submit Epic Challenge, spend its CP and receive Precision. These selected cases explicitly supply the selected-to-fight context. The task-local canonical World Eaters consumer selects and completes the regular Fight activation with the accepted retained grant. Natural Epic Challenge submission survives lifecycle restore and adds Precision. The native Lord profile is proved separately by the selected tests.

Native based former geometry and distances agree with saved pre-destruction geometry. The retained Demise check preserves the same authenticated former footprint across cleanup and rejects using unauthenticated missing death evidence.

Native physical cases include the Wave Serpent and Maulerfiend. Former physical geometry and distance are verified. The test does not independently assert a baseless non-vehicle admission and compare it with a vehicle having a base.
The multi-model native unit rejects measure-to-destroyed-unit while incomplete, then uses the exact final casualty where the first and last distances differ.

Explicit retention checkpoints exercise real Fight completion and phase-end expiry. The retained base is removed before Deadly Demise, former geometry persists, and separate waiting enemy retention survives. Native adapter FNP continuation has restore, fork and exact replay.

Two distinct wounded group orders appear on the opponent request. The test then drives one supplied order through the real advancement helper. Neither option is actually submitted in this selected check.
Both legal opponent-order variants place every wounded group before the unwounded one. Actual casualty mutation advances through that priority.
The native attack logs its saving die before the explicit D0 callback's recorded replacement, then enters Resolve Damage with zero wound loss.

The authenticated retained native Lord can submit Epic Challenge, spend its CP and receive Precision. These selected cases explicitly supply the selected-to-fight context. The task-local canonical World Eaters consumer selects and completes the regular Fight activation with the accepted retained grant. Natural Epic Challenge submission survives lifecycle restore and adds Precision. The native Lord profile is proved separately by the selected tests.
The dice owner yields one D6 per requested unit hazard across every face. The native Infractor resolver fixture records one dice event for its single equipped Hazardous weapon.

A fixture that explicitly requests six hazards resolves one dice event with all six values and the two failed indexes. Bounded to batching already-required rolls at the dice owner. Physical multiweapon selection and mixed-unit damage are separately qualified.
Both unit_hazard and hazardous_test produce a single six-sided die, equal failure outcomes for each of the six faces, and matching failed indexes.

The real rules-unit evaluator assigns one mortal per failure to constructed native-body mixed Vehicle/Infantry and Vehicle/Mounted attachments, with all-Monster/Vehicle controls at three. The separate single-weapon application case verifies real health and allocation. A mixed attachment taking multiple actual failed hazard dice was not exercised.

An explicit multi-die request produces one batch and the constructed mixed attachment uses the correct cost per failed die. There is no combined mixed-attachment run driven by multiple physical Hazardous weapon selections.

The native equipped supercharge resolver fixture records the expected failure, mortal and allocation events. On failure it destroys the wounded non-bearer and leaves the equipped bearer's health unchanged. Success controls preserve both.

A unit hazard request directly asserts one die. The real resolver for a native multi-model Infractor unit accepts the one-die injection for one selected supercharge weapon and asserts one dice event and one mortal on a failing face.
Start-round window precedes the two turns. Constructed Blessings permission produces a real effect before Command completes.
Exact event list puts both complete turns between the round boundaries.
Round end follows both turns and the first finisher cannot terminate round five.
Real round-start Blessings decision and persisting effect in rounds one and two with explicit permission on an admitted native body. Named World Eaters admission is outside the witness.
Both preselected first-player alternatives recur without switching. The fixture writes turn_order at a battle checkpoint, so mission setup selection still needs an independent binding.
Opponent takes the second turn in both orders. The first player's Fight completion hands over to opponent Command in the same round.
Exact event sequence and completion list for start, all five phases and end for four turns. Independent in-turn transitions preserve round and player.
Each turn has a start event before Command. The two-round facade does not assert an eligible nonempty start-turn effect applying.
Command occupies its prescribed place in each facade turn. This maps phase ordering, with eligibility and actions reviewed in the owning phase categories.

Turn-end resolution_order and typed participant consumption establish priority. Both types of production callback completing in the same turn is still unasserted here.

Typed candidates cover both players plus order. Native mission-boundary discovery and evidence are checked in separate active-player fixtures, Reconnaissance has positive VP, and repeated discovery is idempotent. Separate Punishment controls prove both roles are evaluated and a non-active mission owner can actually score five points on its opponent’s turn. No same-boundary pair of achieved missions after a nonempty production non-mission callback is asserted.
Exact recurring windows plus real round-start and unqualified Fight-start effects. No nonempty start-turn hook is asserted by this family and the Fight test drives explicit checkpoints.
Real unqualified Fight-start effect at all four phase checkpoints with the same granting owner, scoped to each active turn. A separate unqualified turn-effect witness remains outside this family.
Round-end label and typed non-mission-first participant ordering pass. No co-triggered real round-end mission scoring callback is asserted.
Round-end metadata and typed priority are supported. A real achieved round-end mission commit is unproven. See mission reachability for the unassigned legacy primary rows.
Facade advances to round three with original first player. Direct GameState checks rounds one and four advance and round five terminates with no active turn.
The explicit compiled start effect actually commits before Core CP on the owning turn. The opposite active-player control leaves the effect unused.
Core CP is after the start effect and before Battle-shock completion. Both players receive one CP across round and actor variants despite re-entry. The same CP is spendable through the normal ledger.

CP precedes Battle-shock and the body request requires completed Battle-shock. The direct native Infractor owner checks carried shock against Leadership, clearance or preservation, and one completion across re-entry.

The body opens after Battle-shock and before the end window. Two body CP effects commit in the chosen order before the end effect. Wrong owner, stale request and early/wrong-phase guard inputs preserve state.
Compiled Command-end effect follows the abilities window. Real loaded end-of-Command rules finish and primary points commit before Movement. The two active-player roles are tested independently.

The selected native-body harness compiles the explicit start, during and end texts, checks the owning actor and timing, and shows no second gain after continuation. This is a constructed source permission, with production compilation and execution.

The unqualified compiled Command effect executes inside the named abilities window after CP and Battle-shock. Start and end effects use their separate windows. This validates the registered CP effect family and routing.

The real sequencer exhausts both typed player occurrences before either typed mission in four cases. The exception is confined to Command end. Native Tormentors produce two sticky mutations before the active primary score, with persisted and forked continuations and exact replay.

Both mission owners continue in the typed policy contract. In the loaded native scene, after both sticky mutations one achieved active primary commits 5 VP or 4 VP in opposite role configurations, with the inactive ledger at zero. Native discovery shows no mission participant in its sticky ordering batch. No admitted defined primary rule in the inspected packs permits a simultaneous inactive Command-end award. Retain the conditional two-award verification as unsupported by the inspected primary assignments.

Constructed compiled effects execute before selection or after Shooting completion and before phase exit in separate actor and timing cases. Independent native attacks resolve inside the body before a next unit request. A single case does not combine both nonempty windows and attacks.

The compiled start effect commits one CP before the selected-unit event for its owner, with opposite active-player and end-timing controls. The source wording is constructed to exercise the production timing route.
The compiled end effect commits one CP after Shooting completion and before phase completion for its owner. Opposite active-player and start-timing cases bound the result to this timing route.

Native control selects one friendly unit, commits and resolves its attacks before a next selection, and guards invalid actor, stale or foreign selections. The controller can end Shooting while other eligible units remain.

Reserved and embarked units are absent. Rejected choices keep state. A selected weaponless or targetless unit cannot select again after taking its type even without attacks, and an attacking unit finishes before next selection.
Exact native selectable-type sets vary with actual engagement and a recorded Advance status. Real engagement-distance controls cross the governing boundary with Normal versus Close-quarters choices.
A native Assault choice yields a matching accepted physical pool, resolves the attack sequence before another unit is offered, and admits a legal Assault weapon after rejecting a non-Assault weapon.

Comparable unengaged and non-Advanced native profiles expose Normal only or distinct Normal and Indirect choices according to native equipment. A selected native Doomweaver then produces an Indirect Fire pool alongside the visible-target ordinary weapon pool. The original live source requires having a weapon, and the split-target test is only a positive corroboration of that eligibility check.

Physical engagement permits a selection with normal or Overrun options according to the recorded start state. A unit now outside engagement reaches real attacks through Overrun in independent start-engaged and constructed charge-permission cases. Without current engagement, start eligibility or charge permission it is absent. The preceding Charge phase is outside these checkpoints.

All four native eligible units resolve distinct attacks before consolidation in both active-player configurations after four accepted no-move Pile In choices. Invalid attacks do not record completion and the legal retry does. The separate consolidation owner accepts declining all four and leaves placement unchanged.

Exact choice actor, unit and band are checked across no grants and both one-sided and two-sided priority permissions. The first-band owner is skipped when only the opponent has priority, and a remaining request follows when priority empties. A witnessed Overrun separately makes a previously ineligible priority unit take the next request.

Initial Remaining actor and alternation are verified, and four normal activations finish before consolidation. A late eligible priority unit correctly receives the next request. The one-pass endpoint proves an exhausted opponent case with a pass. An unequal Remaining inventory with an exhausted actor skipped without a prior pass was not explicitly exercised.

Native geometry allows passing only at 5.001 inches in the 4.999/5/5.001 boundary matrix. A nearby otherwise eligible friendly forbids passing even with a far unit. Two consecutive passes or one against an exhausted opponent advance to consolidation. A normal opponent Overrun can instead bring a target inside five inches, and the passer subsequently attacks.
Native eligible models in Light or Dense are Hidden at the first-turn checkpoint with no prior shooting. Current or preceding shooting is excluded, with source-eligible area and keyword controls.

Both occupied-endpoint permutations exempt the same area. A thin strip leaving a real open line yields partial visibility. A native forbidden declaration is rejected atomically and can decline. The constructed sightline shapes bound the geometry claim.

Aligned Dense windows block up to three inches and a line above the cap remains open. The existing 2.5-inch base plus half-inch body reaches the exact plane. The open/Light counterexamples and native rejection are also asserted. Mixed-angle native timing remains outside this proof.
At a distance within 15 and outside 12, the real targeting consumer reduces reach only when a native model is Hidden and a Dense feature actually intervenes.
The native comparison needs actual intervening Dense geometry, not merely any Light feature or a Dense feature outside the line. The accepted short-range variant also verifies incomplete visibility.
A constructed permission keeps Hidden throughout. Actual targeting then distinguishes current/previous shot history from older or first-turn evidence, so Hidden alone cannot bypass the exclusion.
The native resolution endpoint checks below, exactly at and above 15 inches, then the same boundary at 12 inches for Gone to Ground.
The same area polygon membership holds at ground and elevated checkpoints. The native admitted Frame's constructed offset uses an actual mission terrain polygon.
An overhanging Frame part alone is within the polygon at both heights. Equivalent base-only measurement excludes the same Frame.

The archived requirement says the same positive-OC model must be in range. The unchanged adopted text predicates range on the unit and positive OC on a member, consistent with Order 109. The native-body checkpoint proves an in-range OC0 body and an out-of-range OC-positive attached member can control a friendly-controlled objective. The companion overlap control confirms the same in-range model supplies its complete OC to both results. The absence of such a member or missing range rejects unit control. Historical wording remains preserved and requires evidence-inventory reconciliation.

The normal Movement continuation emits the control record before an admitted compiled end-phase CP effect. Independent phase-end and turn-end entries freeze one snapshot before further work and preserve it across a later occupancy reversal. Only the phase-end example executes a nonempty downstream effect in these controls.

Using native bodies and a constructed authorized secured state, the real boundary keeps the owner at zero and at a tie, and removes retained authority when enemy OC is strictly greater. The saved record and retained ownership persist through serialization and actual boundary commit.

The actual Explosives submission rolls six dice, inflicts one mortal per 4+, reduces the native target to zero wounds and leaves unrelated models unchanged. The state fragment round-trips. This prepared scene does not certify roster or whole-game replay.
The own-turn proposal is denied. The real opponent Fight trigger follows a completed enemy attack sequence in the existing facade control and in the paired native Overrun probe.

The normal reaction identifies two eligible friendly units. Wrong-viewer, stale context and enemy-target inputs preserve the original state. Binding an eligible friendly unit succeeds, including one newly engaged through the paired Overrun.

The selected unit receives Fights First on the spent stratagem. The probe's emitted effect carries the exact target and active owner's Fight-end expiration. Expiry in a completed Fight phase was not exercised.

The paid stratagem activates the chosen unit next, but immediately commits the first legal fight type. For a newly engaged target, the legal set is Normal and Overrun. In the paired ordinary declaration the owner is offered both. Paying for the selected unit skips the mandatory eligible-type choice and reaches ordinary melee.

Each explicit Aircraft/Fortification keyword excludes an otherwise identical native-body control. Titanic does not exempt either keyword. A previously offered action is rejected after each keyword changes, with state and queue preserved. The tags are controlled fixture inputs rather than a play-through with a native Aircraft or Fortification roster.

Typed prior-Advance or prior-Fall-Back movement receipts cause different exact eligibility reasons and reject the previously legal public request atomically. Quick positive controls use the same body with no prior movement. The earlier Movement phase is outside these checkpoints.

An existing action start makes the unit ineligible, rejects stale submission without mutation, and prevents a second same-turn start after completion. The real turn-end Cleanse control on both player assignments independently verifies exact one-time effects and points. Full prior-turn/setup replay is outside these fixtures.

A native leading weapon grant survives bodyguard loss but drops when its leader dies. Independent compiled leader and support grants end at the respective final source casualty. The target-restriction control proves retained support presence under a different source and route. The same leader/support weapon grant through last-source attack death and through the end of all attacks is unasserted.

The compiled Bodyguard grant reaches every living component when one source model remains, then drops at the final source casualty. This is the reserve/checkpoint source-lifetime route. Taking the last bodyguard casualty from an attack and expiry only after the attacker finishes all attacks were not exercised.

A constructed unit-wide weapon grant bound to actual equipped native wargear survives an unrelated casualty and disappears when its bearer is killed by the normal rule-caused model-destruction owner. The reserve checkpoint also binds grant recovery to the same revived model. The test does not exercise an attacking-unit attack sequence.

In four independent role/item variants the real healing decision revives the named exact model in reserves, restores its source across the surviving native attachment and preserves attachment identity. Revival permission is constructed to test the consumer, with no new native datasheet-provider assertion.

Setup choices account for embarked points and accept exact cap versus rejecting one over across three sizes using supplied fixture costs. A cumulative 600+401 declaration against a 1,000 cap is rejected without mutation whether submitted together or after an existing reserve declaration.

At an explicitly selected terminal boundary the native reserve bodies lose all remaining health and placement even under a prior round-deadline exemption. An arrived control survives. The deadline policy and application were exercised directly; a full mission progression to the final turn was not exercised.

Final reserve death leaves the pending return queue empty. The carrier-and-cargo variant additionally asserts the complete decision event log is identical across application. No case first demonstrates that a seeded, admitted model-destruction rule would otherwise trigger for the same body, and no final-turn facade handoff is supplied.

The native Terminator selects the Combi-weapon group before the Combi-bolter group in ordinary Shooting. Actual normal Combi-bolter damage precedes the applied Devastating mortal event in the same attack sequence. The existing critical kernel independently proves no save and no spill across models. The fixture begins in Shooting and does not replay prior game setup.

The Fire Dragon's accepted physical pool snapshots whether its target is within half range. The Exarch removes the only in-half-range model before the later attack. Actual requested damage on the original near branch still includes Melta 3, while a far declaration has zero bonus. The native damage dice and applied damage are read from their matching attack-context histories.

The native Night Spinner physically equipped twin shuriken catapult offers decline and reroll for an initial 1 and an initial 6. The accepted branches share the original roll and physical weapon identity, emit distinct decline/reroll events and each completes the attack. Seeded fixtures are prepared Shooting states, without a full-roster replay claim.

The native leading grant reaches every living component. Native model-only Lone Operative recipients are exactly the source model. The paired constructed whole-unit targeting form reaches every living attached model, and absent source leaves neither recipients nor the target restriction. Wargear lifetimes and other attached abilities are separate.

relevant_entries.body: Yes. For example, if an ability gave a unit +1 OC until the end of the turn, at the end of the turn, that unit would still have +1 OC. That unit would not have +1 OC at the start of the next turn.
relevant_entries.title: If a rule's effect lasts until the end of a specific part of the battle (e.g. until the end of the phase, until the end of the turn), is that rule still in effect at the end of that part of the battle?

shock_disembark_diagnostic.scope_and_qualification: Conditional Core 18.07 and its application of FAQ62, from a constructed Command checkpoint with explicit permission and embarked cargo on current native datasheets. No faction grant or setup proof, broad FAQ62 credit, selected test admission, or addition to the historical counts.
